panels.title: Instance
panels.description: Angles version and Node runtime reported by the scraped instance. Sourced from the angles_build_info gauge, whose value is always 1 - the information is in the labels.

panels.title: API up
panels.description: Prometheus target health - whether the last scrape of /metrics succeeded.

panels.title: Database
panels.description: Whether the Mongo connection is usable. When this is 0 the scrape still succeeds but every database-backed metric is omitted, so panels below will show No data rather than zero.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the Angles process started. A repeatedly resetting value means the container is restarting or crash-looping.

panels.title: Requests/sec
panels.description: Total request throughput across every route.

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: Share of responses returning 5xx. `clamp_min` keeps an idle instance from dividing by zero, and `or vector(0)` makes an instance that has served no 5xx at all read as 0 rather than "No data" - on a headline health tile, an empty panel is indistinguishable from a broken one.

panels.title: p95 latency
panels.description: 95th percentile request latency across all routes. histogram_quantile is 0/0 -> NaN when no requests were served in the window, which is honest for a percentile (there is no p95 of zero requests) - the NaN is mapped to "No requests" so an idle instance does not read as broken.

panels.title: Builds
panels.description: Total builds stored across every team and status.

panels.title: Executions
panels.description: Total test executions stored. This is normally the largest collection.

panels.title: Screenshots
panels.description: Total screenshots stored.

panels.title: Baselines
panels.description: Visual baselines configured for image comparison.

panels.title: Teams
panels.description: Teams configured.

panels.title: Users
panels.description: User accounts.

panels.title: Builds by status
panels.description: Stored builds broken down by status. These are gauges over what is currently in the database, so the series step down when the cleanup cron deletes old builds - they are not cumulative counters.

panels.title: Executions by status
panels.description: Stored test executions by status.

panels.title: Builds by team
panels.description: Stored builds per team. Cardinality is capped by ANGLES_METRICS_MAX_SERIES (default 200); beyond that only the largest series are reported. Builds whose team has been deleted appear as "unknown".

panels.title: Last build per team
panels.description: How long ago each team last submitted a build. This is the panel that catches a silently stopped pipeline - nothing is failing, so no error-rate alert would fire, but builds have stopped arriving. Red past 24h.

panels.title: Request rate by route
panels.description: Throughput per matched route pattern. Routes are labelled by pattern (/rest/api/v1.0/build/:buildId), never raw URL, so build ids cannot create a series each.

panels.title: Request rate by status class
panels.description: Responses per second grouped by HTTP status code.

panels.title: Latency percentiles
panels.description: Request latency distribution across all routes. Buckets run to 120s to cover image-engine work, so the top of the scale is meaningful.

panels.title: p95 latency by route
panels.description: Per-route p95. Screenshot upload and image-compare routes are expected to sit well above the read endpoints.

panels.title: Requests in flight
panels.description: Requests being handled concurrently. A rising floor means work is arriving faster than it completes.

panels.title: Top routes by error rate
panels.description: 5xx responses per second, by route. Empty is the healthy state.

panels.title: 4xx by route
panels.description: Client errors per second. A spike on one route usually means a misconfigured client or expired API token rather than a server fault.

panels.title: CPU usage
panels.description: Process CPU time, as a percentage of a single core - derived from the counters with rate(), so it is correct regardless of scrape interval. 100% means one core fully consumed; the host may have more (see angles_host_cpus).

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Process memory. RSS is the number a container memory limit acts on. Image buffers land in 'external', outside the V8 heap, so a compare-heavy workload grows external and RSS without moving heap much.

panels.title: Event loop lag
panels.description: Delay between a timer being due and running. This is the saturation signal that matters most for Angles: CPU-heavy image work blocks the loop and shows here well before requests start failing. Sustained above ~1s means the API is starved.

panels.title: Host load average
panels.description: Host load average against the logical CPU count. Load sustained above the CPU-count line means the host is oversubscribed - which on a shared box may be something other than Angles.

panels.title: Host memory
panels.description: Host memory split into used and free. Stacked, so the top of the stack is total physical memory.

panels.title: Disk used
panels.description: Filesystem utilisation for the screenshots and compares volumes. Angles writes image data to both; a full screenshot volume stops uploads entirely.

panels.title: Disk available
panels.description: Bytes available on each volume. The downward slope is the useful part - extrapolate it to estimate time-to-full.

panels.title: Angles storage used
panels.description: Bytes Angles itself has written to the screenshot and compare directories. Requires ANGLES_METRICS_DISK_USAGE=true - otherwise this panel is empty by design, since the directory walk costs O(files).

panels.title: Stored files
panels.description: File count in the screenshot and compare directories. Also requires ANGLES_METRICS_DISK_USAGE=true. A count that only ever rises means the cleanup cron is not reclaiming anything.

panels.title: Scrape duration
panels.description: Time taken to build the /metrics response. Rises when the domain cache expires and the Mongo aggregations re-run, and when ANGLES_METRICS_DISK_USAGE walks the image directories.

panels.title: Domain cache age
panels.description: Age of the cached database aggregations. Expected to saw-tooth up to ANGLES_METRICS_CACHE_TTL_MS (default 60s). A value that climbs past the TTL and keeps going means collection is failing and the usage numbers above are stale.

panels.title: Collection errors
panels.description: Rate of failed collection passes. Any sustained non-zero value means the domain metrics are being served from a stale cache.
